quarterly_data.signal: H1 2026 (DART half-year report filed 08-13-2026, consolidated, reviewed by Ernst & Young Han Young): revenue KRW 747,289M vs KRW 461,233M in H1 2025 (+62.0%); gross profit KRW 180,044M (24.1% GM vs 4.9%); operating profit KRW 121,575M (16.3% margin) vs an OPERATING LOSS of KRW 4,335M a year earlier and vs KRW 49,061M for ALL of FY2025; net income KRW 103,177M vs a loss of KRW 1,292M; basic EPS KRW 2,003 vs -25. Q2 ALONE: revenue KRW 400,975M (+63.1% YoY vs KRW 245,858M; +15.8% QoQ vs Q1 KRW 346,314M), operating profit KRW 70,276M (17.5% margin, vs KRW 1,866M in Q2 2025 and KRW 51,298M in Q1 2026), net income KRW 57,675M. Operating cash flow KRW 166,301M (vs 22,872M); cash KRW 84,358M plus KRW 139,996M short-term financial instruments; borrowings only KRW 7,795M (KRW 30,000M Woori Bank short-term loan repaid); dividends paid KRW 25,767M. MIX: single PCB segment (package substrates FCBGA/FCCSP/FCBOC/CSP/SiP for memory and non-memory chips plus MLB for AI servers, network and test equipment); product sales KRW 769,692M less KRW 22,403M intercompany. AVERAGE EXPORT PRICE KRW 1,952,699 per m2 vs KRW 1,444,025 in FY2025 (+35%, mix shift to high-end substrates); domestic KRW 2,660,562 vs 2,444,562. GEOGRAPHY (H1 2026 vs H1 2025): Korea KRW 401,199M (242,668M), China KRW 144,447M (92,645M), US KRW 96,072M (63,338M), Vietnam KRW 20,516M, Taiwan KRW 10,347M, other KRW 74,708M (35,872M); channel split domestic 4%, local export 51%, direct export 45%. Filing text names AI data centers and servers, edge devices, robots, autonomous driving and high-speed communications as the structural PCB demand drivers. Share price average rose from KRW 48,905 in January 2026 to KRW 153,871 in June 2026.
quarterly_data.figure: H1 rev KRW 747.3B (+62.0% YoY); OP KRW 121.6B (16.3%) vs loss; Q2 rev KRW 401.0B (+63.1% YoY, +15.8% QoQ), Q2 OP KRW 70.3B (17.5%); export ASP +35%

quarterly_data.signal: Orders and customers (DART half-year report filed 08-13-2026, as of 2026-06-30): H1 2026 NEW ORDERS 490 thousand m2 / KRW 1,077.7B, DELIVERED 378 thousand m2 / KRW 744.9B, ORDER BACKLOG 112 thousand m2 / KRW 332.8B at 2026-06-30 (~0.8x Q2 revenue; the filing notes the business runs on short-lead-time build-to-order with almost no long-term orders, so only the half-year order total and period-end backlog are stated). CUSTOMER CONCENTRATION (anonymised, >=10% of consolidated H1 revenue): customer A KRW 135,447M (18.1%), customer B KRW 121,293M (16.2%), customer C KRW 106,215M (14.2%) - top three = 48.6% of revenue; a year earlier A was KRW 89,853M, B KRW 65,360M and a customer D KRW 51,441M, so customer B nearly doubled and customer C is newly above the 10% threshold. NAMED MAJOR CUSTOMERS: Samsung Electronics, SK Hynix, Amkor Technology Korea and STATS ChipPAC Korea. Sales are direct, build-to-order (domestic cash/credit, exports by purchase confirmation and T/T); strategy: strengthen partnerships with large domestic customers, expand overseas telecom and network-equipment accounts, focus on high-value products. Customer prepayments: NON-CURRENT CONTRACT LIABILITIES (advances received for point-in-time performance obligations) jumped to KRW 54,828M at 2026-06-30 from KRW 6,762M at 2025-12-31, with land and buildings pledged (KRW 112,237M set) as a guarantee for the contract liabilities under a Hana Bank credit agreement approved by the board on 2026-06-18. Sales representation agreements pay 1-3% of collections on Singapore, Malaysia and Israel sales.
quarterly_data.figure: H1 new orders KRW 1,077.7B; backlog KRW 332.8B at 06-30-2026; top-3 customers 48.6% (A 18.1%, B 16.2%, C 14.2%); customers Samsung, SK Hynix, Amkor Korea, STATS ChipPAC Korea; non-current customer advances KRW 54.8B (from 6.8B)

quarterly_data.signal: Capacity and capex (DART half-year report filed 08-13-2026): H1 2026 PCB capacity 466 thousand m2 (monthly 77,600 m2 across Korea and Vietnam plants; FY2025 1,002 thousand m2), production 393 thousand m2, UTILISATION 84% (up from 76% reported for Q1 2026 and 759/1,002 = 76% for FY2025). Three investment programmes: (1) machinery and equipment April 2022 to December 2027, KRW 270.0B, in progress; (2) BUILDING EXPANSION and ancillary facilities May 2026 to December 2027, KRW 213.0B, in progress (board approved 2026-05-11); (3) FUTURE PLAN: machinery and equipment July 2026 to December 2027, KRW 497.0B - the board resolved on 2026-07-20 (post-period event, disclosed as a new facility investment) to invest KRW 497,000,000,000 by 2027-12-31 in production equipment and ancillary facilities 'to respond to increased semiconductor market demand'. Combined programme = KRW 980B. H1 2026 PP&E additions KRW 124,086M (vs KRW 32,523M in H1 2025), cash capex KRW 108,076M (vs 28,781M); construction-in-progress KRW 172,093M at 2026-06-30 vs KRW 93,100M at 2025-12-31; land purchases KRW 11,867M (B1 parking-lot site approved 2026-01-19); outstanding purchase commitments for PP&E KRW 97,663M. Inventories rose to KRW 203,316M from KRW 148,608M (raw and subsidiary materials KRW 105,253M vs 67,139M) and an inventory write-down reversal of KRW 5,206M was booked (vs a KRW 3,581M write-down in H1 2025). Facility-investment reserve KRW 240,000M in equity.
quarterly_data.figure: Utilisation 84% (from 76%); capex programmes KRW 270B (to 12-2027) + KRW 213B building (05-2026 to 12-2027) + NEW KRW 497B (board 07-20-2026, to 12-31-2027); H1 PP&E additions KRW 124.1B; CIP KRW 172.1B

quarterly_data.signal: R&D and corporate events (DART half-year report filed 08-13-2026): R&D spend KRW 9,468M in H1 2026 (1.27% of sales). Completed development items listed in the filing: high-density C4 bump process for 20k-bump-per-unit FCBGA mass production; LARGE-BODY FCBGA (120 x 150 mm, 26-layer, 2.7 mm thick core) substrate technology; mSAP line/space 9/12 um; fine bond finger 45-pitch and 50-pitch substrates; ultra-thin coreless 3-layer 70 um and 75 um substrates and 4-layer 105 um thin substrate; Cu-pillar 55-pitch fine-pitch bump; via-on-Cu-post 2-layer ETS substrate; Low-Df build-up material for high-end FCB substrates; DTC (deep-trench capacitor) embedding in cavity-structure PCB; thick-core hole plugging over 1.2 mm; domestic mSAP seed copper foil; S-parameter measurement and simulation infrastructure; high-layer thick antenna substrates. Corporate: new subsidiary DD ELECTRONICS CANADA, INC. (Toronto, sales service) incorporated in June 2026 (board resolution 2026-05-11), joining sales offices DD USA (California) and Daeduck Electronics Shanghai and the Daeduck Vietnam PCB plant; Siheung City cooperation agreement reported to the board on 2026-03-20; Yoon Sang-won (Seoul National University electrical engineering professor, semiconductor expert) elected independent director and Byun Young-sam (former SK Siltron CEO) elected statutory auditor on 2026-03-26; largest shareholder Daeduck Co. sold shares between 2026-04-06 and 2026-04-21, cutting its stake from 31.46% to 29.51% (National Pension Service 12.66%); credit rating A- reaffirmed by eCredible on 2026-04-14; headcount 2,742 at 2026-06-30. Related-party product sales to Daeduck Vietnam KRW 18,067M and purchases from it KRW 2,744M in H1.
quarterly_data.figure: R&D KRW 9.5B (1.27%); large-body 120x150mm 26L FCBGA and 20k-bump FCBGA developed; Canada sales subsidiary set up June 2026; parent stake cut to 29.51%

quarterly_data.signal: Raw-material supply chain (DART half-year report filed 08-13-2026, H1 2026 purchases): CCL KRW 96,132M (60.38% of raw materials) from LG Chem and Doosan Electronics; PREPREG KRW 40,997M (25.75%) from Doosan Electronics and LG Chem; ABF (Ajinomoto build-up film) KRW 12,496M (7.85%) from Ajinomoto Fine-Techno; other raw materials KRW 9,599M; raw materials total KRW 159,224M. Subsidiary materials: PGC KRW 55,101M (41.29%) from Heesung Catalysts, other KRW 78,359M (58.71%) from Taiyo Ink Products; subsidiary materials total KRW 133,460M. Unit prices per m2: CCL KRW 107,731 (vs 100,872 in FY2025 - the filing cites CCL price increases as the main input-cost change), prepreg KRW 38,271 (37,731), ABF KRW 34,591 (36,611). The filing says CCL and prepreg are sourced from multiple overseas (Japan, Taiwan) and domestic (Doosan Electronics, LG Chem) suppliers so supply liquidity is good, while dry film and ink remain partly import-dependent with localisation progressing. Supplier-finance arrangements exist with some suppliers (Hana Bank purchase-loan facility KRW 60,000M limit, KRW 18,855M used).
